title: AI-generated art helped me finally build my solo tower defense game — Tower Legends
author: Traditional_End_743
selftext:
Hey everyone,

I’m a solo indie developer building games in my spare time—design, code, balancing, and everything in between.

For a long time, the art barrier kept me from getting a real game off the ground. Using AI-generated spritesheets changed that. It allowed me to focus on what I truly love—gameplay, mechanics, progression, and game feel—and finally turn my ideas into a real game.

This is **Tower Legends**, my upcoming tower defense game. It’s still a work in progress, and I’ve included the current trailer with this post.

You can visit the Steam page for more details and visuals:  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5012660/Tower\_Legends/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5012660/Tower_Legends/)

I’d be happy to hear your thoughts on the trailer, the game’s visual identity, and the overall concept. If it interests you, you can also wishlist it on Steam.

For those of you using AI for 2D game assets: **what workflow and tools do you use to produce consistent, game-ready spritesheets?**  
  
Thanks for taking a look!

Saradoc

replies.author: Traditional_End_743
replies.body:
Thanks!  
It's a web app. I use Phaser [https://phaser.io/](https://phaser.io/) as game engine, mostly for the scene system and spritesheets utilities. I then package it with Cordova [https://cordova.apache.org/](https://cordova.apache.org/) for mobile and Pake [https://github.com/tw93/pake](https://github.com/tw93/pake) for desktop.
